title: I-HITL: Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop
abstract: arXiv:2610.35835v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Human oversight is a pillar of AI safety. It is often exercised by a human in the loop (HITL) who approves critical actions taken by an AI agent. AI agents' increasing ability to bypass guardrails, though, raises the question of how to enforce HITL robustly.   We introduce the concept of inalienable human-in-the-loop (I-HITL). An I-HITL protocol ensures that an agent can initiate an action only with explicit human approval, even when the human interacts with a system (e.g., a local agentic harness) compromised by the agent. A strong I-HITL protocol additionally ensures such approval even when an adversarial human attempts to delegate approvals to an agent.   To motivate I-HITL, we report on experiments with a popular agentic wallet platform in which raising an agent's spending cap requires HITL approval via emailed one-time passcodes (OTPs). translated_abstract: 人类监督是人工智能安全的支柱，通常由一个“人在回路”（HITL）中的人类来执行，由其批准AI智能体采取的关键行动。然而，AI智能体绕过安全防护栏的能力日益增强，这引出了一个如何稳健地强制执行HITL的问题。我们提出了“不可剥夺的人在回路”（I-HITL）的概念。I-HITL协议确保智能体只有在获得人类明确批准的情况下才能启动某项行动，即使人类所交互的系统（例如本地智能体工具框架）已被该智能体攻破也是如此。强I-HITL协议还额外确保，即使对抗性的人类试图将批准权委托给智能体时，行动仍需获得人类的明确批准。为论证I-HITL的必要性，我们报告了在一个流行的智能体钱包平台上的实验：在该平台中，提高智能体的消费上限需要通过电子邮件发送的一次性密码（OTP）进行HITL批准。在可以访问用户电子邮件且任务因消费上限而受阻的情况下，我们发现十个不同的前沿（模型）……
tldr: 该论文提出“不可剥夺的人在回路”（I-HITL）协议，确保即使智能体攻破了人类所交互的系统、甚至人类试图将批准权委托给智能体时，智能体的关键行动仍必须获得人类明确批准才能执行。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop (I-HITL) protocol, which guarantees that AI agents can initiate critical actions only with explicit human approval, even when the agent compromises the system the human interacts with or an adversarial human attempts to delegate approvals to the agent.
